request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for surgical treatment of cecal cancer with sclerosing mesenteritis. The surgery involved a right colectomy with excision of a diffusely thick mesenterium with multiple yellowish nodules. Pathology report revealed Astler-Coller C2 cecal adenocarcinoma and diffuse sclerosing mesenteritis of the excised mesenterium. The patient followed oncologic treatment consisting in capecidabine under close surveillance of his coagulation parameters with no reported abdominal pain or discomfort. A CT scan was performed 6 months later in the context of cancer follow-up, which did not demonstrate any significant radiological changes of the sclerosing mesenteritis.

History and Physical:
An 83-year-old male was admitted with a past medical history of atrial fibrillation, coronary heart disease, and previous surgeries including an appendicectomy in his childhood and a laparoscopic cholecystectomy three years ago. He presented with symptoms of weight loss, abdominal discomfort, and persistent fatigue leading to a complete laboratory examination demonstrating iron deficiency anemia.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Plan:
The patient underwent a right hemicolectomy. Oncologic treatment with capecidabine was initiated post-surgery, and the patient was discharged with close follow-up appointments. 

Disposition:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.

Follow-up:
The patient is advised to follow up with his oncologist for continued cancer surveillance.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode was an admission for surgical treatment of cecal adenocarcinoma, a right hemicolectomy. The sclerosing mesenteritis was found incidentally on pathology, and the iron deficiency anaemia was a presenting finding caused by the cancer. The cancer is therefore the condition chiefly responsible for the admission.

Cecum is coded to C18 (malignant neoplasm of colon), with C18.0 for the caecum.

CODE: C18
